subject: Deferred provisioning opt-in + price-safety request for committed tier
messages:
From: Emma Green <emma.green@novasutra.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@novasutra.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deferred provisioning opt-in & request for price-safety on committed tier

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We like Redwood's performance profile but NovaSutra is sensitive to public GPU market swings — our board wants protections if market GPU spot/contract prices spike during our 24-month committed term.

Two asks to explore:
- An opt-in for deferred provisioning (ability to stagger actual activation of reserved pool across tranches) so we don't pay for idle capacity if we choose to delay ramping.
- A price-safety mechanism: either a credit / rebate if GPU input costs behind your reserved SKU increase > X% vs benchmark, or an explicit pass-through cap.

We're willing to lock a multi-quarter minimum commit but need guardrails on cost exposure. I attached our internal mandate (novasutra_mandate.pdf) and a short ramp plan.

Can you sketch the typical options Redwood offers here and any approvals required? We're on a timebox for procurement next week.

Thanks,
Emma Green
Head of Platform Ops, NovaSutra
emma.green@novasutra.com

---
Attachment: novasutra_mandate.pdf (PDF stub, 120KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Green <emma.green@novasutra.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@novasutra.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deferred provisioning opt-in & request for price-safety on committed tier

Emma — thanks for the clear note and the mandate. Looping in Marissa (account lead) and Laura (finance) to validate commercial feasibility and approval path.

High level (two pragmatic approaches we can offer):

1) Staggered activation (deferred provisioning opt-in)
   - You commit to the full reserved amount and term, but we allow activation in up to 4 tranches over the first 12 months. Unactivated capacity sits in a non-billable holding state for the first 90 days per tranche; beyond that we either bill a reduced standby fee or permit reallocations.
   - Pros: predictable headline pricing, preserves pool for you; Cons: small standby fee after 90 days, impacts our capacity planning.

2) Price-safety mechanism (GPU input indexation + credit ladder)
   - We benchmark a GPU-cost index at kick (public market index + our supplier contracted index). If our internal modeled GPU-cost per token > benchmark threshold (we typically model 20% bands), we trigger either: 1) a rebate credit applied retroactively to invoices for the quarter, or 2) a capped pass-through where we absorb up to X and pass only beyond.
   - Commercially we can offer a blended SKU discount today and a contingent credit pool that grows with sustained GPU-cost delta.

I've attached a quick sensitivity model (pricing_sensitivity_model.csv) and a proposed activation slate (proposed_slate.xlsx) to make the tradeoffs concrete.

Marissa — can you outline the discount/credit ranges you'd propose to present for NovaSutra? Laura — flag us on the approval ladder (what discount bands need exec signoff vs finance approval).

Next steps: Emma, if you can confirm (A) acceptable max standby window per tranche, and (B) whether you prefer 'credit ladder' vs 'pass-through cap', we'll draft the commercial language and run approvals.

Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

---
Attachments: proposed_slate.xlsx (Excel stub), pricing_sensitivity_model.csv (CSV stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Emma Green <emma.green@novasutra.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deferred provisioning opt-in & request for price-safety on committed tier

Thanks Karthik — quick read of the model and our suggested commercial structure below. Pasting the short version so procurement has something concise: 

Option A — Conservative: 12-month staggered activation + 15% floor discount
- Activation: Up to 4 tranches over 12 months. Each tranche has a 90-day free hold window; after 90 days a standby fee of 6% of tranche value applies.
- Price-safety: 15% baseline discount on committed SKU. If weighted GPU-cost > benchmark by 20-30% for a full quarter, customer receives a 3% rebate (applied retroactively) per quarter of sustained delta, up to an additional 9% annual rebate (cap).
- Approval: Marissa can approve this without exec escalation.

Option B — Protective: Deferred opt-in + stronger contingent credit (preferred by customer if they want protection)
- Activation: Same tranching but with an extended 150-day free hold for first tranche only.
- Price-safety: 12% baseline discount + contingent credit pool sized at 5% of committed ARR that triggers when GPU delta > 15% and paid as quarterly credits. If the credit pool would exceed 20% equivalent discount in a year, we need C-suite signoff.

Recommendation: Start with Option A in the term sheet to keep approvals light, include a table that allows NovaSutra to elect Option B before signing (opt-in checkbox). That gives them comfort and keeps our exposure capped.

Emma — if that sounds directionally OK, I can build the exact contract language (service schedule + pricing appendix). Laura please confirm approval bands below so I can mark them in the draft:
- Up to 15% blended discount: account team approval.
- 15–20% blended discount or contingent-credit pools >5% ARR: finance approval (Laura).
- >20% blended discount or structural pass-throughs: CPO/CFO signoff required.

Marissa
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Folks — reviewed Marissa's options and the sensitivity model. Practical approval path below so we can move to legal/Docusign: 

- I can approve up to an 18% blended discount (or equivalent credit pools up to 5% of committed ARR) under standard underwriting. For anything requiring a >18% hit to our unit economics we need CFO/CPO signoff; allow 48 hours turnaround if both are available.
- Standby fee structure as described is fine; please ensure the 90/150 day windows are reflected as explicit lifecycle states in the SOW so billing can be automated.
- For the indexation trigger, legal wants: (a) a public benchmark source (we recommend the combined market index in the spreadsheet), (b) quarterly reconciliation, and (c) bilateral audit rights limited to pricing reconciliation only.

Emma — if you can confirm which option you want to table into the term sheet (A vs B), we will:
1) Insert the pricing appendix with the chosen tier,
2) Run finance signoff (I will queue the approval), and
3) Send the first DocuSign envelope; HubSpot will be updated once signoff complete.

Laura Bennett
